chapter: Growing up in the Thirteenth Ward
title: His parents and the death of his brother
summary: His parents were Walter Lawrence Cotton and Edna May Lanz of Baton Rouge; a brother was killed by a truck as a boy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So what was your mother's name?
Her name was Edna. Edna May Lanz before she married my dad. His name was Walk the Lawrence Cotton. Okay.
And he was from New Orleans? Yes.
He was from New Orleans but she was from Baton Rouge. She was from Baton Rouge. She came down with her folks and he met her. Okay.

Well I had a brother who was at 616 Bell Castle Street. He was out there playing ball with Alfred Collins and some other guys. He ran after the ball. The man's backing out didn't see him and the truck ran over him. He got crushed. And it wasn't too long after that that we moved back to 822 Bell Castle. And like I said my dad he left and we stayed there until 1968 and we moved over. That single house that we acquired back then in 1978 and we got this 822 where we first, when my mother saw the address up there.
